SectionHead draft

The numbered head that opens a section: a serif italic number in the live accent with a short accent underline, alone in its own column beside an h2 title and an optional lede, the title's first line on the number's baseline; on narrow viewports the number and the title share one row and the lede runs full width below. One layout, no variant, no states — the page places it.

Variants: — · A11y: pending

No states: nothing hovers, nothing focuses (RFC §3.3). The title's first baseline sits on the number's at every width (adoption checkpoint 2B / 5B); at a viewport width of 768px and below the number and the title share one row and the lede runs full width below — the one media query, in section-head.css, restating --ll-breakpoint-md (§3.4). The <em> rendering of the title (§7 Q8) is proven by the local suite, not shown as a docs example: an element-valued prop has no JSX snippet form in the docs generator yet. The stacked heads of Fundamentals and the landing stay product compositions (LL.Eyebrow + title + text, §7 Q1).

RFC: SectionHead.rfc.md · Figma node: 109:9

Guidelines

Golden rules

  1. One layout, always an h2. The number in its own column beside the title, the title's first line on the number's baseline; at 768px and below (--ll-breakpoint-md) the number and the title stay on one baseline row, s-2 apart, and the lede runs full width below. The heading level is always 2 — no level, layout or size option (RFC §7 Q1, Q10, checkpoint rows, adoption checkpoint 2B / 5B).
  2. The number is order, not meaning. num is required and rendered verbatim, hidden from assistive technology: the document order (and the role guides' table of contents) already give it (RFC §7 Q2, Q9). The product computes it — two digits by convention, "01" … "11".
  3. The title wraps. No single-line rule: a long or translated title wraps instead of overflowing (RFC §7 Q7, WCAG 1.4.10). An <em> in it renders italic in the live accent (§7 Q8).
  4. The page places it. The component ships no margin, padding or width: the <section>, its anchor id, its spacing and the page grid are the product's (RFC §2.3, §3.4).

Do

  • Pass the section number as a string the product formats ("01"): the component never pads or computes it (§3.1).
  • Give id to name the section: <section aria-labelledby="phases"> with <SectionHead id="phases" …> — the id lands on the h2 (§3.1, §4.1).
  • Keep the section's own anchor id (the TOC target) on the product's <section>, not on the head (§3.1).
  • Put the lede in lede, not after the component: it sits s-15 under the title and is left out entirely when omitted (§7 Q11).
  • Use h3 for the headings inside the section: the head is the h2 (§7 Q10).

Don't

  • Don't put an Eyebrow, the number or any label inside title — the h2's accessible name stays the title alone (§4.1; Eyebrow §7 Q9).
  • Don't rely on the number being announced: a product that needs it voiced writes it into the title, where it joins the heading's name (§4.3).
  • Don't force the title onto one line or truncate it (§7 Q7).
  • Don't override the number's size, the underline or the column width product-side — one recipe (§7 Q3–Q6).

Props

PropTypeDefaultOptionalNote
num string — no required: the section's number, rendered verbatim in its own column and hidden from assistive technology (RFC §3.1, §7 Q2, Q9). Two digits by product convention; the product computes it, the component never formats it
title ReactNode — no required: the heading text, rendered inside the one h2; may hold an <em>, rendered italic in the live accent (§7 Q8); wraps freely (§7 Q7). Never an Eyebrow, the number or any label inside it (Eyebrow §7 Q9)
lede ReactNode — yes the introductory paragraph under the title, type/body in fg/dim (§7 Q11, Q12); omitted (or empty) → no <p> is rendered at all
id string — yes forwarded to the h2, never to the root, so the product can name its <section> with aria-labelledby; omitted → no id attribute anywhere in the component (§3.1). The section's own anchor id stays on the product's <section>

Accessibility pending

Semantic structure
Exactly one root <div class="ll-section-head"> (no role) holding, in DOM order, one <span class="ll-section-head-num" aria-hidden="true"> whose text is num verbatim, then one <div class="ll-section-head-body"> holding exactly one h2 and, only when lede is given, one p (RFC §3.4, §4.1). The heading is always an h2 (§7 Q10) whose accessible name is the title alone: the number sits outside it and is hidden unconditionally (§7 Q9). id, when given, lands on the h2 only. The root is a div, not a header: inside a <section> a header maps to no landmark.
Keyboard
Nothing to do: no interactive element, nothing focusable — no a, button, input or tabindex is rendered by the component (RFC §3.3, §4.2). The aria-hidden number holds text only, so aria-hidden-focus has nothing to find. Interactive content in title or lede is not expected; if the product nests a link it keeps its own semantics, product-side.
Decisions
Contrast is computed by the gate from resolved tokens, never declared here: the title fg/default, the lede fg/dim, the number and the title's <em> accent/default, each on bg/default — pairs already declared in contrast-pairs.json at normal-text (stricter than the large text the 44px number and 32px title need), the accent pair scored once per accent (RFC §4.3). The aria-hidden number is still visible text: WCAG 1.4.3 applies and the declared pair covers it. The underline is decoration (no text), exempt, no pair. The title wraps — no nowrap — and the body column is minmax(0, 1fr) with overflow-wrap: break-word, and at a viewport width of 768px and below (--ll-breakpoint-md) the lede takes the full width under the number–title row, so nothing overflows horizontally (WCAG 1.4.10). Under that breakpoint the body wrapper is display: contents — a bare div with no role and no attribute but its class, so no semantics can be lost (locked by the suite); the DOM and reading order never change.
Notes
Implemented per RFC §4; this status moves to pass only through the accessibility engine gate, never by assertion.
